test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Why does a skilled cricketer move his hands backwards while catching a fast-moving ball?

options.text: To apply a greater opposing force on the ball for a quick stop.
To reduce the force by increasing the time over which momentum changes.
To increase the speed of the ball during impact.
To decrease the weight of the ball using gravity.

solution:
The correct answer is __**To reduce the force by increasing the time over which momentum changes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a cricketer moves his hands backward while catching a fast-moving ball, the time duration of the impact increases. This results in the momentum of the ball changing more gradually.
 
• According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, force is inversely proportional to the time over which the change in momentum occurs. Increasing the time reduces the force applied on the hands.
 
• Reducing the force during impact helps in minimizing the risk of injury to the cricketer's hands.
 
• This technique utilizes the concept of "Impulse," which is the product of force and the time duration of its application.
 
• The backward movement of hands ensures that the ball's momentum is brought to zero in a controlled manner, enhancing the efficiency and safety of the catch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**

 
 
• Newton's Second Law states that Force (F) = Mass (m) × Acceleration (a). It also relates to momentum as F = Δp/Δt, where Δp is the change in momentum and Δt is the time interval.
 
• The concept of impulse is derived from this law, where Impulse = Force × Time = Change in Momentum.
 
 
 
• **Momentum:** Momentum (p) is the product of an object's mass and velocity (p = mv). It is a vector quantity and is conserved in the absence of external forces.
 
• **Impulse:** Impulse is the measure of the change in momentum of an object when a force acts over a time interval. It explains the importance of increasing the time of impact to reduce the applied force.
 
• **Safety in Sports:** Techniques like moving hands backward while catching are designed to minimize injuries by distributing the force over a longer time, aligning with the principles of physics.
 
• **Real-World Applications:** The same principle is applied in car crash safety mechanisms like airbags and crumple zones, which increase the time of impact to reduce force and prevent severe injuries.
